Apps can trust an identity provider such as Entra ID instead of storing passwords locally
Identity providers replace encryption, so apps should disable TLS

explanation: A central identity provider authenticates users and issues tokens. Local password stores in every app are not a security requirement and increase credential sprawl.

stem: An application needs a TLS certificate and a database connection string at runtime, and developers must not check those values into Git. Which Azure service is designed to store both?

choices.text: Azure Key Vault, which stores secrets, keys, and certificates

explanation: Key Vault stores secrets, keys, and certificates so apps retrieve them at runtime instead of embedding them in source control. Access reviews, PIM alerts, and Content explorer are not secret stores.

stem: A hub must filter TCP/UDP flows between virtual networks, while a public website also needs inspection of HTTP cookies and request bodies. Which pairing is accurate?

choices.text: Azure Firewall filters network flows; Azure WAF inspects HTTP application requests
Azure WAF is the only service that can filter virtual-network TCP flows in a hub
Azure Firewall recertifies guest users, and WAF issues MFA challenges
Firewall and WAF are both Microsoft Defender for Identity sensors

explanation: Azure Firewall is a network-layer (and related) traffic filter. WAF inspects HTTP application payloads. They address different layers and are not identity sensors.

stem: A public website stays online during a large volumetric flood, but users can still be phished by a fake sign-in page. What does that illustrate about Azure DDoS Protection?

choices.text: DDoS Protection helps availability against floods; it does not by itself stop identity phishing or application-layer abuse
DDoS Protection replaces Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication
DDoS Protection classifies and encrypts SharePoint files
A surviving public IP means Conditional Access is no longer required

explanation: DDoS Protection is an availability control against volumetric attacks. It is not an identity, labeling, or phishing control.

stem: An NSG allows TCP 443 to a web subnet. Attackers then send SQL injection in HTTPS bodies. Why might that NSG still be insufficient?

choices.text: NSGs decrypt TLS and therefore already block injection
An allow-443 NSG is equivalent to Microsoft Entra ID Protection
NSGs filter ports and addresses; they do not inspect HTTP application payloads the way a WAF does
SQL injection is remediated only by Service Trust Portal reports

explanation: NSGs are network allow/deny filters. Application-layer inspection of HTTP payloads is a WAF job. Opening 443 does not imply payload inspection.

subobjective: Describe network segmentation with Azure virtual networks
stem: A payment workload must not share the same private address space as a general development environment. Which Azure construct provides that isolation?

choices.text: A Temporary Access Pass issued to the payment subnet
Separate virtual networks or subnets that segment the workloads

explanation: Virtual networks and subnets segment Azure resources into isolated private address spaces. TAP, compliance score, and Defender TI do not create network isolation.

stem: Administrators need browser-based RDP to Azure VMs. Why is Azure Bastion a different answer from a site-to-site VPN?

choices.text: A VPN is the Microsoft service that opens RDP on every public IP
Bastion is an identity provider, and a VPN is a sensitivity label
Bastion and VPN are both names for Microsoft Entra Conditional Access
Bastion provides managed RDP/SSH over TLS to VMs without exposing RDP/SSH ports; a VPN extends network connectivity rather than replacing that managed jump host

explanation: Bastion is a managed jump-host service for RDP/SSH over TLS. A VPN connects networks; it is not the SC-900 control that removes public RDP/SSH from VMs.

stem: A company publishes an Azure web app and wants managed rules that catch common OWASP web attacks. Which service is the fundamentals fit?

choices.text: Azure Web Application Firewall associated with the published web front end

explanation: WAF managed rules protect published web applications from common HTTP attacks. Access reviews, PIM, and records management do not inspect web requests.

stem: An Azure subscription already has posture recommendations. Security also wants Microsoft 365 email, device, and identity incidents in one XDR queue. Why is Defender for Cloud not that XDR queue?

Defender for Cloud is the Microsoft Defender portal incident queue
Defender for Cloud replaces Defender for Office 365 Safe Links
Defender for Cloud is Microsoft Entra ID

CSPM is the only Microsoft EDR sensor

Defender for Endpoint is only for Azure SQL databases
Defender for Servers replaces Microsoft Entra ID Protection

Defender for Cloud recommendations recertify Entra guest groups

Manual response means hashing has replaced SOAR
SIEM detection without SOAR automation leaves repeatable response steps manual
The SOC must switch to records management to automate containment

stem: A company wants one SIEM to ingest Microsoft 365, Azure, and third-party firewall logs. Why is Microsoft Defender XDR not a complete substitute?

Defender XDR is the only Microsoft service that can store firewall syslog
Third-party firewall logs can be ingested only by Azure Bastion

explanation: XDR is optimized around Microsoft Defender workloads. Sentinel is the SIEM that can connect many data sources, including non-Microsoft logs.

subobjective: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel
stem: Leadership asks whether Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender XDR are the same product. Which distinction is accurate?

choices.text: Defender XDR is the only Microsoft SIEM, and Sentinel is only a WAF
Sentinel replaces Entra ID, and Defender XDR replaces Azure virtual networks
They are identical names for Compliance Manager
Sentinel is a cloud SIEM/SOAR that can ingest many sources; Defender XDR correlates Microsoft workload signals into a unified incident view

explanation: Sentinel is SIEM/SOAR across diverse logs. Defender XDR natively correlates Microsoft 365 Defender workloads. They integrate but are not the same control.

stem: Which service is not a Microsoft Defender XDR workload in current SC-900 training?
explanation: Defender for Endpoint, Office 365, and Identity are XDR workloads. Azure Firewall is an Azure network control, not a Defender XDR workload.

source.title: What is Microsoft Defender XDR? - Microsoft Defender XDR

stem: Safe Attachments detonates email files in a sandbox. Safe Links checks URLs when users click them. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: Safe Links replaces Safe Attachments, so file detonation is never needed
Both features are Azure Firewall DNAT rules
They are complementary Defender for Office 365 controls for files versus URLs
Safe Attachments is a Conditional Access named location

explanation: Safe Attachments and Safe Links address different email/collaboration objects: files and URLs. Current SC-900 training treats both as Defender for Office 365 capabilities.

source.title: Why do I need Microsoft Defender for Office 365? - Microsoft Defender for Office 365

stem: A workstation needs behavioral blocking and forensic investigation of a running process. A domain controller needs detections for ticket theft. Which pairing is accurate?

choices.text: Defender for Identity is the laptop EDR agent
Defender for Endpoint analyzes Kerberos ticket attacks on domain controllers as its primary job
Both needs are met only by Azure WAF
Defender for Endpoint for the workstation EDR; Defender for Identity for Active Directory identity attacks

Defender for Cloud Apps detonates mailbox attachments as Safe Attachments
Defender for Cloud Apps for the CASB/SaaS problem; Defender for Office 365 for email and collaboration threats
Both problems are solved only by Azure Key Vault

explanation: CASB and email protection are different Defender workloads. Cloud Apps is not Safe Attachments, and Defender for Office 365 is not the shadow-IT inventory.

source.title: Overview - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps

stem: A learner says Microsoft Defender for Identity is the tool that synchronizes on-premises users into Entra ID. What is the accurate correction?

Entra Connect is an XDR email workload
Hybrid identity sync is Entra Connect (or related sync); Defender for Identity detects identity attacks in Active Directory
Pass-the-ticket detections require password hash synchronization to be disabled

explanation: Entra Connect (and related hybrid identity tooling) synchronizes identities. Defender for Identity is a threat-detection workload for Active Directory, not the sync engine.

source.title: Microsoft Defender for Identity Overview - Microsoft Defender for Identity

stem: A device has an unpatched browser CVE. A mailbox has a malware attachment. Which pairing is accurate?

choices.text: Safe Attachments closes CVEs on endpoints
Defender Vulnerability Management ranks the software weakness; Defender for Office 365 handles the email malware
Both needs are met only by Azure DDoS Protection

explanation: Vulnerability management is exposure and weakness prioritization. Email malware is Defender for Office 365. They are not interchangeable.

The Purview portal investigates endpoint process trees
Microsoft Defender portal for XDR operations, Purview portal for compliance, Azure portal for Azure resource security
The Azure portal is Microsoft's only eDiscovery console

explanation: Those portals align to different jobs: XDR operations, compliance/data governance, and Azure resource management. They should not be treated as one interchangeable console.

stem: A manager says CSPM will detect a running malware process on a VM the same way EDR does. What is the accurate correction?

CSPM assesses configuration posture; detecting running threats on a workload is cloud workload protection or endpoint detection
CSPM is only a retention label
CSPM issues FIDO2 keys to virtual machines

explanation: CSPM is misconfiguration and standards posture. Runtime threat detection belongs to workload protection or EDR, not to CSPM alone.

Analytics rules are SIEM detection; playbooks are SOAR automation
Analytics rules are Azure Bastion sessions

stem: Defender XDR can automatically disrupt an in-progress attack across workloads. How should a learner contrast that with a SIEM that still needs an analyst to run a playbook?

A SIEM always automatically disables Entra users with no configuration, and XDR cannot contain anything
XDR is only a WAF, and a SIEM is only a retention label
They are the same because both are Azure Key Vault

Defender for Office 365 only protects Azure public IPs
Email attachments are filtered only by network security groups

Replacement of Azure Key Vault for certificate issuance
Replacement of Defender for Endpoint sensors
App and session visibility or control inside cloud apps, beyond the initial access decision

From Active Directory environment signals, commonly via sensors aligned to domain controllers or AD FS
From Purview retention label analytics only
From Service Trust Portal audit PDFs only

stem: SOC analysts hunt across Defender XDR alerts in one operations console. A compliance officer needs Microsoft audit reports about Microsoft's own services. Which pairing is accurate?

The Defender portal publishes Microsoft's ISO audit PDFs as its primary job
Both jobs are done only in Azure Bastion
Microsoft Defender portal for XDR operations; Service Trust Portal for Microsoft's audit and trust documents

stem: Defender for Cloud can show regulatory-control status for Azure resources. Compliance Manager assesses the customer's implementation of compliance controls. Why switch products for those jobs?

choices.text: Compliance Manager remediates NSG rules as its primary job
Azure/multicloud regulatory posture lives in Defender for Cloud; customer compliance assessments live in Purview Compliance Manager
Defender for Cloud is the only place to complete GDPR improvement actions for Microsoft 365
They are the same score stored in Azure Bastion

Safe Links is Microsoft's actor encyclopedia
Both jobs are Azure Key Vault certificate issuance
Defender Threat Intelligence provides actor and infrastructure context; Safe Links is the email time-of-click control

Privacy means Microsoft must disable MFA so support can read mailboxes
Privacy is achieved by publishing NSG allow-all rules

Privacy principles are Microsoft's data-handling commitments; Compliance Manager tracks customer improvement actions against assessments

The Purview portal publishes Microsoft's SOC reports as its primary job
Both jobs are done in Azure Bastion
Service Trust Portal for Microsoft's audit reports; Microsoft Purview portal for the tenant's DLP configuration

Those Purview solutions are reached from the Microsoft Purview portal, not from Entra identity administration
eDiscovery holds are Conditional Access grant controls

Microsoft-managed actions recertify Entra guest groups
The split means the customer no longer owns any data
Microsoft implements some controls for its service; the customer still completes remaining improvement actions

explanation: Compliance Manager distinguishes Microsoft-implemented service controls from customer improvement actions. SaaS does not finish the customer's compliance work.

subobjective: Describe the uses and benefits of compliance score
stem: A manager treats compliance score as a pass/fail exam result that proves the company is certified. What is the accurate correction?

choices.text: A score of 100 is Microsoft's official ISO certificate
Compliance score replaces the need for the Service Trust Portal
Compliance score is Defender for Cloud's only secure-score value
Compliance score estimates remaining improvement-action progress; it is not itself a certification or exam grade

explanation: Compliance score is a prioritization metric inside Compliance Manager. It does not certify the organization or replace Microsoft audit reports.

stem: Classification found credit-card numbers. A learner says that finding already encrypts the files. What is missing?

choices.text: Sensitive information types automatically issue FIDO2 keys
Classification identifies sensitive items; protection still requires labels, DLP, or other controls that act on those findings
Finding a pattern deletes the file, so encryption is unnecessary

explanation: Classification answers what exists and where. Encryption, labeling, and DLP are separate protection decisions.

subobjective: Describe the benefits of Content explorer and Activity explorer
stem: Content explorer shows where labeled items live. Activity explorer shows labeling, sharing, and DLP events. Why are those explorers not DLP policies?

choices.text: Content explorer blocks outbound credit-card numbers as its primary job
Explorers provide visibility; DLP policies detect and help prevent risky sharing
Both explorers are Azure Firewall application rules

explanation: The explorers answer where content is and what happened to it. They do not replace DLP prevention policies.

subobjective: Describe sensitivity labels and sensitivity label policies
stem: Which two protection outcomes can a sensitivity label apply to a document in addition to classifying it? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Encryption and access restrictions that travel with the file
Visual markings such as headers, footers, or watermarks
Azure DDoS Protection for the author's public IP

explanation: Sensitivity labels can encrypt content and apply markings. They are not DDoS or PIM controls.

stem: A file is labeled Confidential and encrypted, but a user can still paste the same credit-card numbers into a Teams chat. Which control is missing?

choices.text: Azure DDoS Protection on the Teams tenant
Data loss prevention policies that detect and restrict sensitive sharing in locations such as Teams
Azure Bastion for the Teams client

explanation: Labels can protect a document. DLP watches sharing channels such as Teams for sensitive information types. Encryption on one file does not automatically DLP the chat channel.

stem: Security wants the same credit-card DLP check in Exchange email, SharePoint, Teams, and on endpoints. What should the learner expect?

choices.text: DLP policies can apply across multiple locations rather than only one mailbox
DLP exists only as an Azure NSG application rule
DLP can run only after a file is declared a record
Endpoint DLP is a Conditional Access grant control

explanation: Purview DLP is designed to cover multiple locations including email, sites, chat, and devices. It is not an NSG, a record requirement, or a Conditional Access grant.

stem: A records team needs a scheduled review before a declared record can be disposed of at the end of its retention period. Which records-management idea is that?

choices.text: Disposition review, which can require approval before a record is destroyed
Azure WAF custom rules that delete SharePoint items
Microsoft Entra access reviews of VM start rights

explanation: Records management can require disposition review so records are not silently deleted when the retention period ends. WAF, Entra access reviews, and Safe Links are not records disposition.

source.title: Records management for documents and emails in Microsoft 365

subobjective: Describe the uses and benefits of compliance score
stem: Which two elements does Compliance Manager use when it helps an organization understand remaining compliance work? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Improvement actions the customer still needs to complete
A compliance score that estimates progress against recommended controls

explanation: Compliance Manager combines improvement actions and a compliance score to prioritize remaining customer work. DDoS SKUs and FIDO2 inventory are not Compliance Manager elements.

stem: DLP blocked a credit-card number in email. Separately, a departing employee downloaded thousands of unlabeled files over two weeks. Which tool is designed for that second pattern?

choices.text: Insider Risk Management, which looks for risky user behavior patterns, not only a single DLP match

explanation: DLP is policy matching on sensitive content. Insider Risk Management looks at sequences of potentially risky user activity such as departing-employee exfiltration.

subobjective: Describe eDiscovery solutions in Microsoft Purview
stem: Legal needs mailboxes preserved for a lawsuit even if users try to delete messages. How does that differ from a routine retention period?

Retention holds are the only way to respond to a lawsuit
eDiscovery hold is a Conditional Access grant control
A lawsuit is preserved only by Azure Firewall

explanation: Legal hold is an eDiscovery preservation action for a matter. Retention policies serve ongoing lifecycle requirements. They can coexist but they are not the same decision.

subobjective: Describe audit solutions in Microsoft Purview
stem: Investigators ask who changed a DLP policy yesterday and from where. They do not need to export an entire mailbox for court. Which Purview capability answers that?

choices.text: Azure Bastion session recording of the mailbox
Audit logging of user and admin activities

explanation: Purview audit records who did what, when, and where. Exporting a mailbox for court is eDiscovery. Bastion, lifecycle workflows, and DDoS reports are not that activity trail.

source.title: Learn about auditing solutions in Microsoft Purview

stem: A customer must show progress against ISO 27001 improvement actions in their own tenant, not download Microsoft's ISO report. Which tool is that customer-side tracker?

subobjective: Describe the benefits of Content explorer and Activity explorer
stem: An investigator knows a file was labeled Highly Confidential this morning and then shared externally. Which explorer shows that activity timeline?

subobjective: Describe sensitivity labels and sensitivity label policies
stem: Users should see Confidential markings on documents, but not every label defined in the tenant. Which statement is accurate?

Every label in the tenant is always visible in Word
Network security groups publish labels to Word

stem: Email must be kept for seven years, but the same mailbox must still be prevented from sending credit-card numbers. Which pairing is accurate?

DLP is the keep-or-delete lifecycle engine
Retention keeps content for the required period; DLP prevents risky sharing of sensitive information
Both needs are met only by Azure Bastion

All three are Azure Bastion features

Conditional Access is a subset of Insider Risk Management file plans
Insider Risk Management analyzes internal user activity patterns; Conditional Access still evaluates sign-in conditions
Insider Risk Management issues FIDO2 keys

DLP policies can be created only in Azure Bastion
Exchange DLP is a network security group
